source.title: Contrastive Learning with Growing Generated Representations for Inductive Knowledge Graph Embedding
source.authors: Qian Li; Linje Cui; Shafiq R. Joty; Da-Ling Wang; Shi Feng; Yi-Fei Zhang; Chengwei Qin

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling analysis to inductive knowledge-graph embeddings and reports link-prediction performance as representation capacity is varied; it does not reproduce language-model loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study reports no language-model held-out cross-entropy, parameter/token/compute sweep, or compute-optimal allocation results. Its own scaling results concern H@1 on inductive knowledge-graph link prediction and are recorded for V6; its discussion of language-model scaling laws is background.
record.test_reason: The study varies capacity in an inductive knowledge-graph embedding model (VMCL+CAT): meta-KG count, embedding dimension (8 to 32) and number of generated representations. It reports link-prediction H@1 in figures only. It trains no language model, reports no held-out loss, fits no power law and does no compute-optimal analysis. Kaplan and Hoffmann appear only in related work, where the authors say their results 'align with the scaling behavior'. Its scaling results concern a different kind of system and measure, so they go under fits_no_version rather than V5 or V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors say VMCL beats baselines and 'exhibits scaling abilities with increasing scale'. In related work they frame this as smooth scaling rather than emergence. They also report saturation, both after 3 generations and for Outside meta-KGs, which the paraphrase only partly mentions.
record.recipe_differences: This is an inductive knowledge-graph embedding study using link-prediction H@1, not a language-model pretraining-loss scaling study. It varies meta-KGs, embedding dimension, and generated representations rather than language-model parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The scaling curve depends on which capacity is increased and on whether results are Outside (PT only) or Inside (PT and FT); generation-count gains flatten after the initial increase.

fits_no_version.finding: In an inductive KG-embedding model, H@1 rises with meta-KG count, with dimension (approximately linearly over 8 to 32) and with generated representations. Gains saturate for Outside meta-KGs and after 3 generations. Results are figure-only, with no fitted functional form.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Link-prediction accuracy of inductive KG-embedding models improves monotonically, with saturation, as embedding dimension, pretraining subgraph count and augmentation count grow.

record.problems: Scaling values are shown in figures without reported uncertainty estimates. The dimension settings conflict: Section 6.3 lists 16, 32, 64, 128, while Section 6.5 and Fig. 6(b) give 8, 16, 32.

untested.parts: Not tested: no language-model held-out loss is measured against parameters, tokens or compute.
Not tested: there are no fits and no extrapolation to larger runs.
Not tested: there is no compute-optimal allocation analysis.
Not tested: shape is not varied at a fixed parameter count.
Not tested: KG embeddings are a different regime, but no power-law form is fitted or tested.
Not tested: there are no language-model downstream tasks, and nothing is predicted from pretraining loss.
Not tested: no exponents are fitted and fitting choices are not compared.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' with V6 labels overreaches. V6 concerns language models' downstream performance, and this paper's capacity sweeps are on a small KG-embedding model with no power-law fits. The cited Kaplan and Hoffmann work is background only. The paper's settings conflict with each other: dimensions are 16 to 128 in Section 6.3 but 8 to 32 in Section 6.5, and the meta-KG list includes 20000 in only one of the two places.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation from smaller language-model runs to larger runs.
Architecture changes at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the study does not fit or test power laws.
Language-model downstream tasks and performance predicted from pretraining loss are not tested.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: VMCL+CAT

conditions.value: Fig. 6(a); text describes the general trend without enumerating the datasets for this result

rows.note: The text says H@1 first rises substantially and then tends to stabilize; on F1 it rises from 5% to 60% and then slowly increases to 70%.
rows.check: This measures KG-embedding link-prediction H@1, not a language model's loss or downstream score, and no power law is fitted. State describes the rise then plateau (F1: 5% to 60%, then about 70%). Section 6.3 lists 20000 meta-KGs, which Section 6.5 omits.
